text: Starting in MongoDB 5.2, `$group` can run in SBE when it is the first pipeline stage or every preceding stage can also run in SBE. This condition establishes eligibility for `$group`; later unsupported stages can still prevent the whole pipeline from running in SBE. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

The current MongoDB time-series query README lists SBE-lowering conditions: unpacked fields must be statically known, the pipeline must not sort on the timeField or use the last-point optimization, and event and meta filters must use SBE-supported expressions. If a condition fails, the entire pipeline runs in classic. If the conditions pass, SBE lowers the supported prefix; the whole pipeline runs in SBE only when every stage is supported. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

MongoDB's SERVER-71032 issue describes a query that was eligible for SBE but whose plan still fell back to the classic engine when SBE plan construction did not produce a usable plan. This is a historical implementation case from 2022, not evidence that every current release has the same fallback behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2022-11-02)

SBE should not be treated as a universal speedup. MongoDB documentation describes improved performance in most cases, while a 2026 study comparing MongoDB 6.0.3 and 8.2.5 reports results varying by aggregation shape, including faster $match plus $group tests and slower unbounded $project tests. The study compares server versions and does not isolate SBE as the cause of those differences. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-31)

SBE eligibility does not guarantee better performance. MongoDB's manual says SBE improves performance and reduces CPU and memory costs in most cases. A 2021 MongoDB server issue reported up to 30% regression for small point queries during SBE plan construction; that is a historical, workload-specific result, not a current baseline. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2021-01-22)

A May 2026 benchmark of a synthetic aggregation workload reported that `$match` plus `$count` used `COUNT_SCAN` on MongoDB 6.0.3 and SBE `GROUP` on MongoDB 8.2.5, with 4 ms measured in each setup. This example shows a version-dependent execution path for one query shape; it does not establish behavior or performance for time-series workloads. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-15)

Confirm the engine that actually ran with explain or slow-query logs. SBE explain output includes `queryPlanner.winningPlan.slotBasedPlan`; slow-query logs use `queryFramework: "sbe"` or `queryFramework: "classic"`. MongoDB's aggregation guide also identifies `GROUP` and `EQ_LOOKUP` stages as SBE signals. (high confidence)

Verify the engine used for the specific operation: SBE explain output includes explain.queryPlanner.winningPlan.slotBasedPlan, and slow-operation logs identify the framework with queryFramework: "sbe" or queryFramework: "classic". Explain ignores the plan cache, so it reports the plan chosen for that explain run. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

Engine availability also depends on distribution: Percona Server for MongoDB 6.0 release documentation lists upstream change SERVER-94166 as disabling the SBE query engine in its 6.0 line. Check the deployed fork and release instead of assuming upstream MongoDB eligibility rules imply SBE is enabled. (medium confidence)

MongoDB selects an execution engine per query. SBE eligibility depends on support for the query's operators and expressions; ineligible queries use the classic engine, and the supported surface changes by server version. An independent SBE implementation account also describes a deliberately limited virtual-machine instruction set, which is consistent with operator coverage acting as an eligibility boundary. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

Percona's release notes for Percona Server for MongoDB 6.0.17-14 list SERVER-94166 as disabling SBE in that 6.0 fork. This is specific to that Percona build and does not describe the upstream MongoDB engine-selection default. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-09-18)
